item.content:encoded:
Tulane University is inviting applications for an 18-month Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence, beginning on January 5, 2027, in New Orleans, Louisiana.

Hosted by the Department of Communication at Tulane University, the position is designed for early-career researchers whose scholarship examines the changing relationships between technology, society, politics, culture, digital media, influence, and the future of work.

The selected Postdoctoral Fellow will become an inaugural affiliate of a developing interdisciplinary initiative focused on the future of work. Through both research and teaching, the Fellow will help contribute to the intellectual foundations of what Tulane describes as a prospective new interdisciplinary center.

The role combines an active independent research agenda with undergraduate teaching, faculty mentorship, participation in departmental intellectual life, and access to Tulane University’s institutional and library resources.

The appointment is full-time for 18 months and carries a 2-2 teaching load, meaning that the Fellow will teach two courses per semester. Tulane emphasizes that the position also includes protected research time so that the successful candidate can continue developing publications and a broader scholarly profile.

Salary will be commensurate with experience, and the position includes a full benefits package.

There is no fixed final application deadline stated in the vacancy. However, review of applications will begin on October 15, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Candidates are therefore strongly encouraged to submit their materials before the first review date.

About the Tulane University Postdoctoral Fellow Position

The Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence is being recruited by Tulane University’s Department of Communication in anticipation of a broader interdisciplinary initiative examining the future of work.

Rather than focusing on one narrow definition of work, the position welcomes researchers studying how contemporary changes in digital technologies, platforms, information systems, media, politics, and culture are transforming the way work is organized, experienced, governed, represented, and monetized.

The successful Fellow will contribute through two complementary areas:

  1. Independent academic research
  2. Undergraduate teaching

The Fellow will also participate in the intellectual development of the emerging future-of-work initiative.

This makes the opportunity especially relevant to scholars interested in combining a traditional academic postdoctoral appointment with participation in a new institutional research agenda.

Position at a Glance

Institution: Tulane University

Department: Communication

Position: Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence

Location: New Orleans, Louisiana, United States

Employment: Full-time

Appointment duration: 18 months

Start date: January 5, 2027

Teaching load: Two courses per semester

Research time: Protected research time included

Salary: Commensurate with experience

Benefits: Full benefits package

Application review begins: October 15, 2026

Closing: Applications continue to be reviewed until the position is filled

Contact: Dr. Vicki Mayer, vmayer@tulane.edu

Research Focus: Technology, Society and the Future of Work

Tulane is particularly interested in researchers whose work can advance critical debates concerning the ways the future of work intersects with technology, society, politics and culture.

The call deliberately leaves room for a wide variety of substantive topics and methodological traditions.

Potential research areas specifically identified by the Department include:

  • Digital employment
  • Work platforms
  • Emerging and new technologies
  • Big data applications
  • Influence campaigns
  • Advertising
  • Political economy of attention
  • Social media
  • Digital policy
  • Changing information environments
  • Technology and labor
  • Digital communication

The list is illustrative rather than narrowly prescriptive.

Applicants whose research connects meaningfully with the broader themes of digital communication, influence, emerging technologies and the future of work may therefore have a strong fit even if their exact project does not use one of these specific labels.

Digital Employment and Work Platforms

One potential research direction concerns the expansion of digitally mediated employment.

Digital technologies increasingly organize how people:

  • Find work
  • Complete work
  • Are managed
  • Are evaluated
  • Communicate professionally
  • Develop careers
  • Build professional identities

Researchers examining digital labor or work platforms could therefore find this position particularly relevant.

Potential topics could include platform economies, algorithmic management, remote work, digital labor, creator economies, online freelancing, gig work or changing relationships between workers and technological infrastructures.

Tulane does not require applicants to work on any one of these topics, but digital employment is specifically included among the areas of interest.

Emerging and New Technologies

The future-of-work initiative also welcomes scholarship examining new and emerging technologies.

This could potentially include research on technological developments affecting:

  • Communication
  • Employment
  • Management
  • Media production
  • Information circulation
  • Organizational culture
  • Political communication
  • Advertising
  • Public discourse

Because the position is situated in Communication, applicants should be able to demonstrate how their work contributes to questions relevant to media, communication, influence, technology or related social processes.

Big Data Applications

Big data is another research area highlighted by the Department.

Researchers may investigate how large-scale data systems are reshaping communication, organizations, platforms, labor practices, surveillance, targeting or decision-making.

Potential questions could involve:

  • Data-driven management
  • Algorithmic systems
  • Digital surveillance
  • Data analytics
  • Targeted advertising
  • Platform governance
  • Data and workplace power

Again, these are potential directions rather than formal requirements.

Influence Campaigns and Advertising

The position places particular emphasis on influence.

Researchers working on advertising, persuasion, political communication, digital influence, information campaigns or platform-based communication may therefore be particularly well aligned.

Influence can operate across multiple areas, including:

  • Political campaigns
  • Commercial advertising
  • Social-media promotion
  • Digital persuasion
  • Branding
  • Influencer cultures
  • Public communication
  • Organizational communication

The successful Fellow may investigate these topics through critical, qualitative, quantitative, computational, historical or mixed-method approaches.

Political Economy of Attention

Tulane also identifies the political economy of attention as a relevant research area.

The contemporary digital environment increasingly treats attention as an economic and political resource.

Researchers may examine how platforms, advertisers, media institutions, creators, employers and other actors compete for and monetize attention.

This could raise questions about:

  • Platform capitalism
  • Advertising systems
  • Algorithmic visibility
  • Monetization
  • Digital labor
  • Audience measurement
  • Media industries
  • Economic power

Candidates whose scholarship examines media and communication through political-economic perspectives could therefore be strong potential applicants.

Social Media Research

Social media represents another major research area.

Potential applicants may investigate how social platforms shape:

  • Work
  • Professional identity
  • Politics
  • Influence
  • Advertising
  • Labor
  • Public culture
  • Information
  • Social relationships

Research could potentially focus on major platforms, emerging media ecosystems or broader social and institutional consequences of platformization.

Digital Policy

Tulane also welcomes scholars working on digital policy.

Relevant questions could include:

  • Platform regulation
  • Data governance
  • Digital rights
  • Online advertising regulation
  • Technology policy
  • Labor regulation
  • Artificial intelligence governance
  • Information policy
  • Platform accountability

This area could be particularly relevant to applicants interested in bridging academic research with policy debates.

All Methodological Approaches Are Welcome

One of the notable features of the vacancy is that Tulane explicitly welcomes:

All methodological approaches

The Department therefore does not require applicants to use one particular form of research.

Potential approaches may include:

  • Qualitative research
  • Quantitative research
  • Mixed methods
  • Computational methods
  • Ethnography
  • Interviews
  • Archival research
  • Historical analysis
  • Textual analysis
  • Discourse analysis
  • Policy analysis
  • Digital methods
  • Critical theory

Applicants should select methods appropriate to their own scholarly questions.

This methodological openness creates space for candidates from a wide range of intellectual traditions within Communication and adjacent disciplines.

Research Expectations

The successful Fellow is expected to maintain an active research agenda throughout the 18-month appointment.

Tulane will provide several forms of institutional support.

These include:

  • Faculty mentorship
  • Workshop participation opportunities
  • Institutional resources
  • Library resources
  • Departmental colloquia
  • Working groups

The Fellow will be encouraged to use the appointment to advance their research and publication profile.

Publication Expectations

The position specifically encourages Fellows to submit scholarly work for publication.

This could include developing:

  • Journal articles
  • Book chapters
  • Manuscripts
  • Conference papers
  • Collaborative research

The vacancy does not specify a mandatory publication quota.

Instead, the emphasis is on maintaining active scholarly productivity appropriate to an early-career academic.

Protected Research Time

Despite the teaching responsibilities, Tulane emphasizes that the Fellow will have protected research time.

This is significant because the appointment is intended to support both teaching development and scholarly advancement.

Applicants should therefore consider how they would use the 18-month period to move their research agenda forward.

A strong application may benefit from explaining:

  • Current research projects
  • Planned publications
  • Future research questions
  • How Tulane’s environment would support the work
  • How the proposed scholarship relates to the future-of-work initiative

Teaching Responsibilities

The Fellow will teach:

Two courses per semester

This represents a 2-2 teaching load.

The teaching responsibilities are divided conceptually into two areas.

Course 1: Fellow’s Research or Methodological Expertise

One course will reflect the Fellow’s own:

  • Research specialization
  • Methodological expertise

This provides the successful applicant with an opportunity to design or teach material closely connected to their scholarship.

Depending on the Fellow’s background, this course could potentially focus on areas such as digital labor, social media, political communication, advertising, platforms, digital research methods, media industries or other relevant subjects.

Course 2: Contemporary Digital Communication and Influence

The second course will address topics connected with contemporary changes in communication and information.

Potential areas identified in the job description include:

  • Digital communication
  • Media influence
  • Advertising
  • Information
  • Persuasion
  • Changing communication landscapes

The Department describes these as topics important to students’ knowledge and skills as they prepare for future careers.

This means the successful candidate should be able to connect academic research with practical and contemporary questions facing students entering media, communication, policy, technology or related professions.

Ability to Teach Undergraduates

Effective undergraduate teaching is an explicit qualification.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate evidence of teaching ability where possible.

This could include:

  • Courses previously taught
  • Teaching assistantships
  • Guest lectures
  • Course design
  • Teaching evaluations
  • Pedagogical training
  • Mentoring students

Applicants without extensive independent teaching experience should still clearly articulate their capacity and readiness to teach at the undergraduate level.

PhD Requirement

Applicants must hold a:

PhD in Communication or a closely related discipline

The doctorate must be conferred by January 5, 2027, the start date of the appointment.

This means candidates who are currently completing their doctorate may apply as long as all requirements will be completed and the degree formally conferred by the appointment date.

Candidates whose PhD will not be completed by January 5, 2027 would not satisfy the published requirement.

What Counts as a Closely Related Discipline?

The vacancy does not provide an exhaustive list of acceptable related fields.

Potentially relevant disciplines could include areas intersecting closely with Communication, digital media, technology, media studies, political communication or related social-science and humanities research.

However, applicants from outside Communication should ensure that their research demonstrates a clear intellectual fit with:

  • Digital communication
  • Media
  • Influence
  • Advertising
  • Future of work
  • Technology and society

Candidates uncertain about disciplinary fit can direct questions to Dr. Vicki Mayer.

Required Research Specialization

Applicants must demonstrate research specialization in:

  • Digital communication
  • Influence
  • Advertising

or a closely related area.

This requirement reinforces the importance of showing a coherent intellectual connection between the applicant’s previous research and the position.

A candidate who works broadly on technology or society should explain clearly how their project contributes to the Department’s communication-centered agenda.

Scholarly Productivity

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

Evidence of scholarly productivity commensurate with career stage

This wording recognizes that postdoctoral applicants may have different publication records depending on when they completed or are completing their PhDs.

Relevant evidence could include:

  • Peer-reviewed articles
  • Book chapters
  • Manuscripts under review
  • Conference presentations
  • Published research
  • Significant working papers
  • Other scholarly outputs

Candidates should organize their CV so that reviewers can easily identify their strongest research achievements.

Preferred Qualification: Interdisciplinary Engagement

Tulane is particularly interested in someone willing to contribute to campus-wide discussions concerning the development of the new interdisciplinary center.

This suggests that the successful Fellow should be comfortable collaborating beyond the Communication Department.

The future of work is inherently interdisciplinary and can involve scholarship from areas such as:

  • Communication
  • Sociology
  • Political science
  • Economics
  • Business
  • Technology studies
  • Media studies
  • Cultural studies
  • Labor studies
  • Public policy

Applicants who can communicate across disciplinary boundaries may therefore be particularly competitive.

Community-Engaged Research

Experience with community-engaged research is considered a plus.

Community-engaged scholarship may involve conducting research collaboratively with communities, organizations or practitioners rather than treating them only as research subjects.

This type of experience could be particularly relevant in New Orleans, where questions concerning work, technology, culture, media, inequality and urban life may intersect in complex ways.

However, community-engaged research is preferred rather than required.

Policy-Relevant Research

Experience producing policy-relevant research is also considered advantageous.

Researchers whose scholarship contributes to conversations around digital governance, platform regulation, information policy, advertising, labor or technology policy may therefore have an additional point of alignment.

This may be particularly relevant for scholars who want their work to engage audiences beyond academia.

Compensation and Benefits

The salary is described as:

Commensurate with experience

No specific salary range is provided in the supplied vacancy.

Applicants should therefore avoid relying on unofficial salary figures unless Tulane publishes additional information.

The appointment includes:

  • Full benefits package
  • Library access
  • Institutional resources
  • Research mentorship
  • Departmental academic opportunities

Appointment Length

The position lasts:

18 months

The appointment begins:

January 5, 2027

The supplied advertisement does not indicate that the appointment is renewable beyond the stated 18 months.

Applicants should therefore plan their research and career development around the published appointment period.

Location

The position is based at:

Tulane University in New Orleans, Louisiana, United States

This is not described as a remote position.

Applicants should therefore expect to relocate to or work in New Orleans for the appointment unless Tulane provides a different arrangement during the hiring process.

Application Materials

Candidates must submit several materials through the official application system.

1. Cover Letter

Applicants should provide a cover letter describing:

  • Research agenda
  • Fit with the position

The cover letter is likely to be one of the most important opportunities to explain the connection between the applicant’s existing work and Tulane’s emerging future-of-work initiative.

A strong cover letter should avoid simply repeating the CV.

Instead, it should explain:

  • What the applicant studies
  • Why the research matters
  • How it fits the future-of-work agenda
  • How the candidate could contribute to Tulane
  • What they hope to accomplish during the postdoctoral appointment

2. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must provide an academic CV.

Relevant sections may include:

  • Education
  • Publications
  • Research experience
  • Teaching
  • Conference presentations
  • Grants and awards
  • Professional experience
  • Service
  • Methods
  • Community engagement

The strongest elements connected to digital communication and the future of work should be easy to identify.

3. Writing Sample

Applicants must submit a writing sample of:

No more than 40 pages

Candidates should select a piece that best demonstrates:

  • Analytical ability
  • Research quality
  • Theoretical contribution
  • Methodological competence
  • Writing quality

Where possible, a writing sample connected to the job’s thematic areas may make it easier for reviewers to understand the applicant’s intellectual fit.

4. Three Recommenders

Applicants must provide:

Names and contact information for at least three professional references

The announcement refers both to recommenders and professional references.

Candidates should therefore identify scholars or professionals who can speak convincingly about their:

  • Research
  • Teaching
  • Academic potential
  • Professionalism
  • Fit for postdoctoral work

The vacancy information supplied does not state that recommendation letters must be uploaded at the initial application stage, only that contact information is required.

Applicants should follow the exact instructions shown in the official portal.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted through the official portal provided for the position.

Application link:
https://lnkd.in/eGa_7ueY

Applicants should ensure all required materials are ready before submitting.

Application Review Date

Review of applications begins:

October 15, 2026

The position will remain open:

Until filled

October 15 should therefore be treated as an important practical deadline even though it is technically the beginning of review rather than a final closing date.

Applicants seeking full consideration should ideally submit their materials before this date.

Contact for Questions

Questions about the academic position may be directed to:

Dr. Vicki Mayer

Email:

vmayer@tulane.edu

Applicants should use this contact particularly for questions concerning:

  • Research fit
  • Position expectations
  • Departmental environment
  • Academic qualifications

Preparing a Strong Application

1. Make the Future-of-Work Connection Explicit

Do not assume reviewers will automatically see how your research fits.

Explain clearly how your scholarship contributes to understanding the future of work.

2. Show Communication Relevance

Applicants from adjacent disciplines should make their connection to Communication particularly clear.

Demonstrate how your research contributes to debates concerning:

  • Media
  • Information
  • Digital platforms
  • Influence
  • Advertising
  • Technology
  • Communication

3. Develop a Coherent Research Agenda

The Department is looking for someone with an active scholarly agenda.

Your application should show what connects your previous work, current research and future plans.

4. Demonstrate Teaching Readiness

Because the position carries a 2-2 teaching load, teaching should not be treated as secondary.

Highlight your ability to teach undergraduate students effectively.

5. Explain What You Could Teach

Although the vacancy does not explicitly request a separate teaching proposal, applicants can strengthen their materials by showing how their expertise could translate into engaging courses.

6. Highlight Publication Potential

Explain what research you expect to develop during the appointment and how the protected research time could support publication.

7. Show Interdisciplinary Capacity

The Fellow will help contribute to a developing interdisciplinary initiative.

Demonstrate that you can communicate productively with scholars outside your immediate subfield.

Why This Postdoctoral Position Stands Out

Several features distinguish this Tulane University postdoctoral opportunity.

First, the Fellow will join at the early stage of a developing future-of-work initiative, creating an opportunity to contribute to its intellectual direction.

Second, the role explicitly welcomes a broad range of methodological approaches.

Third, it combines teaching with protected research time and faculty mentorship.

Fourth, its thematic focus covers some of the most rapidly changing areas of contemporary society, including:

  • Digital labor
  • Platforms
  • Emerging technology
  • Social media
  • Advertising
  • Influence
  • Big data
  • Digital policy
  • Attention economies

Finally, the position offers an opportunity to build both research and teaching credentials over an 18-month period.

Important Details at a Glance

Institution: Tulane University

Department: Communication

Position: Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence

Location: New Orleans, Louisiana

Start date: January 5, 2027

Duration: 18 months

Status: Full-time

Teaching: Two courses per semester

Research: Protected research time

Salary: Commensurate with experience

Benefits: Full benefits package

Required degree: PhD in Communication or closely related discipline by start date

Research specialization: Digital communication, influence, advertising or related field

Review begins: October 15, 2026

Closing date: Open until filled

Contact: vmayer@tulane.edu

APPLY HERE

Conclusion

The Tulane University Postdoctoral Fellow in Communication, Digital Media, and Influence 2027 offers an attractive opportunity for emerging scholars examining how technology, media, culture, politics and society are reshaping the future of work.

Beginning on January 5, 2027, the full-time appointment runs for 18 months and combines undergraduate teaching with independent research, faculty mentorship and participation in a developing interdisciplinary initiative.

Candidates may work across topics including digital employment, work platforms, emerging technologies, big data, influence campaigns, advertising, political economy of attention, social media and digital policy.

Tulane welcomes all methodological approaches, making the position relevant to scholars working across qualitative, quantitative, computational, historical, theoretical and mixed-method traditions.

Applicants need a PhD in Communication or a closely related discipline by the start of the appointment, an appropriate research specialization, evidence of scholarly productivity and the ability to teach effectively at undergraduate level.

The application requires a cover letter, CV, writing sample of no more than 40 pages and contact information for at least three professional references.

There is no fixed final deadline, but review begins on October 15, 2026 and continues until the position is filled. Candidates seeking strongest consideration should therefore aim to submit their application before October 15.

item.content:encoded:
The Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator (AFCIA) 2026, implemented by the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) Innovation Accelerator in partnership with the Adaptation Fund, is inviting organizations with innovative climate adaptation solutions to apply for support to strengthen resilience, improve food security and help vulnerable communities respond to climate change.

The opportunity is particularly focused on Latin America and the Caribbean, with this edition seeking solutions that can be implemented in or have strong potential for implementation in the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Peru.

Applications are open to established organizations developing solutions that address pressing climate adaptation challenges, including climate-smart agriculture, early warning systems, climate information, disaster risk management, water management, climate-risk financing and post-harvest losses.

Application deadline: 6 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.

What Is the Main Goal of the Programme?

The AFCIA programme aims to support innovations that can contribute to a more resilient and sustainable future for communities facing climate-related challenges.

The programme seeks to:

  1. Strengthen climate adaptation and resilience.
  2. Improve food security.
  3. Support vulnerable and climate-affected communities.
  4. Promote gender equity and inclusion.
  5. Create inclusive economic opportunities.
  6. Engage young people in climate adaptation.
  7. Encourage collaboration between innovators and humanitarian organizations.
  8. Expand knowledge and learning around climate adaptation.
  9. Support solutions with potential for large-scale implementation.
  10. Promote sustainable and locally relevant approaches to climate resilience.

Rather than focusing only on ideas at an early conceptual stage, the programme is seeking innovations that have already progressed beyond the idea or early pre-seed phase and have a credible pathway toward implementation and scale.

What Types of Innovations Is WFP Looking For?

The programme is open to both low-tech and high-tech solutions.

This means applicants do not necessarily need to have developed sophisticated or highly technical technologies. What matters is whether the innovation provides a meaningful, scalable and sustainable response to a clearly identified climate adaptation challenge.

Potential solutions may involve:

  • Digital technologies
  • Climate information systems
  • Agricultural technologies
  • Early-warning systems
  • Financing mechanisms
  • Water-management approaches
  • Climate-smart agriculture
  • Disaster-risk management
  • Food-system innovations
  • Market intelligence
  • Communication technologies
  • Community-based approaches
  • Humanitarian innovations
  • Environmental solutions
  • Business-model innovations

The most important consideration is whether the proposed solution addresses a relevant climate adaptation problem and has credible potential for impact and scale.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is designed for established legal entities, rather than individual applicants.

Eligible organizations may include:

  • For-profit companies
  • Non-profit organizations
  • Social businesses
  • NGOs
  • International NGOs
  • Other established legal entities

An organization must also have a presence in at least one of the three countries of implementation: Dominican Republic, El Salvador or Peru.

This presence could include:

  • A country office
  • A permanent operational presence
  • A subsidiary
  • Long-term operations
  • An established partnership in the country

Organizations from outside the three countries may therefore be relevant if they have an appropriate and established presence or partnership structure in one of the target countries.

Key Eligibility Requirements

Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before applying.

The innovation must:

1. Be submitted by an established legal entity

The applicant must be an established organization such as a company, NGO, social business or other legally recognized entity.

2. Have a presence in a target country

The organization should have an established presence in:

  • Dominican Republic
  • El Salvador
  • Peru

3. Address a relevant climate adaptation challenge

The innovation must respond to at least one of the priority areas identified for the country where it will be implemented.

4. Be beyond the idea stage

The innovation must be at least at the seed stage.

Solutions that are still only ideas, research concepts or at the early pre-seed stage are not eligible.

5. Have potential for scale

Applicants should demonstrate a clear pathway for expanding their solution beyond a small pilot.

6. Have adequate resources

The organization must have sufficient resources and capabilities to implement the proposed activities during the nine-month Sprint programme using the available funding.

7. Demonstrate willingness to collaborate

Applicants are expected to have strong intentions to:

  • Collaborate with relevant humanitarian stakeholders
  • Develop relationships with WFP country offices
  • Engage with local innovation ecosystems
  • Work with relevant partners

How Will Innovations Be Evaluated?

Eligible applications will be assessed against several important criteria.

1. Level of Innovation

The proposed solution should demonstrate genuine innovation and respond effectively to climate adaptation challenges within the identified thematic areas.

WFP will consider how novel and innovative the solution is and whether it offers a meaningful improvement over existing approaches.

2. Relevance to the Local Context

The solution must be relevant to at least one of the target countries and its identified climate adaptation priorities.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • A clear understanding of the problem
  • The relevance of the solution
  • The needs of intended users
  • How the innovation fits the local ecosystem
  • The practical value of the solution

3. Financial Sustainability and Scalability

A strong application should demonstrate that the innovation can become financially sustainable.

Applicants should be able to explain:

  • How the solution generates or can generate sustainable revenue
  • How it can continue beyond programme support
  • What its business model looks like
  • How the solution can grow
  • What resources will be required for expansion

Scalability is an important part of the opportunity because the programme is looking for innovations capable of generating meaningful impact beyond a limited pilot.

4. Team Expertise and Capabilities

The strength of the team will also be considered.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Relevant technical expertise
  • Entrepreneurial capabilities
  • Commitment
  • Motivation
  • Ability to implement the proposed solution
  • Technical coherence
  • Appropriate leadership
  • Diverse and inclusive team composition

A strong solution must be supported by a team capable of turning the proposed innovation into measurable results.

5. Climate Adaptation

The innovation should make a meaningful contribution to climate adaptation.

This could involve:

  • Increasing resilience to climate impacts
  • Improving resource efficiency
  • Promoting sustainable practices
  • Helping communities prepare for climate-related shocks
  • Supporting adaptive decision-making
  • Reducing vulnerability to climate risks

6. Level of Impact

Applicants should provide evidence of the solution’s actual or potential impact.

WFP will consider whether the innovation can produce:

  • Tangible results
  • Sustainable improvements
  • Long-term benefits
  • Meaningful climate adaptation outcomes
  • Improvements that can extend beyond the grant or programme period

Historical evidence of impact can strengthen an application, particularly where the innovation has already been tested.

7. Environmental and Social Sustainability

Solutions must align with the environmental and social principles of the Adaptation Fund.

Applicants should therefore consider the broader environmental and social implications of their proposed innovation.

8. Gender and Inclusion

Gender equality and inclusion are important components of the programme.

Applicants should demonstrate how their solution:

  • Addresses diverse user needs
  • Promotes inclusive participation
  • Supports inclusive decision-making
  • Uses disaggregated data where appropriate
  • Incorporates feedback from different user groups
  • Considers the needs of populations that may be disproportionately affected by climate change

Application Process

Interested organizations should first carefully review the official call for applications and eligibility requirements.

The application process involves completing the online application form and providing information about the organization, the innovation, the problem being addressed, the target market or users, the solution’s impact and its potential for scale.

Important Application Deadline

6 September 2026 at 11:59 p.m. UTC.

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their applications. Organizations should allow sufficient time to review the eligibility requirements, develop their responses and ensure that all information submitted is accurate and complete.

Important note: The supplied source contains a typographical error in one instance, displaying the year as “20265”; elsewhere on the same source it clearly identifies the deadline as 6 September 2026. The article therefore uses 2026 as the deadline year.

What Happens After Applications Are Submitted?

According to the programme information, WFP plans to review applications and select approximately 10 to 12 successful applications in November 2026.

Selected organizations will then be invited to an innovation bootcamp in January 2027.

The process can be understood in stages:

Stage 1: Application

Organizations submit their innovation through the online application form by the September deadline.

Stage 2: Evaluation

Applications are reviewed against the programme’s eligibility requirements and evaluation criteria.

Stage 3: Selection

Approximately 10–12 successful applicants are expected to be selected.

Stage 4: Innovation Bootcamp

Selected innovators will be invited to participate in the bootcamp scheduled for January 2027.

Stage 5: Sprint Programme

Following the bootcamp, participating teams will have the opportunity to apply for the Sprint programme.

Stage 6: Funding and Tailored Support

Teams selected for the Sprint programme can receive funding and tailored support from the WFP Innovation Accelerator to help implement, test or scale their solutions.

It is therefore important to understand that submitting the initial AFCIA application does not automatically mean receiving Sprint funding. The programme describes a competitive process involving application, selection, bootcamp participation and a subsequent opportunity to apply for the Sprint programme.

What Is the AFCIA Sprint Programme?

The Sprint is designed as a structured support programme for selected innovators.

During a Sprint, innovators receive support aimed at helping them:

  • Implement their solutions
  • Test key assumptions
  • Validate their approaches
  • Expand their activities
  • Strengthen their impact
  • Work toward scaling their innovations

The WFP Innovation Accelerator provides tailored support to help innovations move from promising concepts and solutions toward practical implementation and greater impact.

Examples of Relevant Innovation Areas

Depending on the target country, organizations working in the following areas may find the opportunity particularly relevant:

  • Climate-smart agriculture
  • Agricultural advisory services
  • Early warning systems
  • Climate information
  • Disaster risk management

  • Climate-risk financing
  • Anticipatory action
  • Food-system resilience
  • Post-harvest loss reduction
  • Market intelligence
  • Climate-risk communication
  • Digital climate services
  • Resource-efficient technologies

However, applicants should consult the official call for applications to determine whether their particular solution falls within the priority areas for the country in which they intend to implement it.

Key Dates and Programme Timeline

Stage Expected timing
Application deadline 6 September 2026, 11:59 p.m. UTC
Selection of successful applications November 2026
Innovation bootcamp January 2027
Sprint programme Following the bootcamp and subsequent competitive selection

The programme information indicates that the Sprint implementation period will involve a nine-month Sprint, with available funding and tailored support for selected innovations.

Language of Application

The current application information states that only applications submitted in English will be accepted.

Applicants should therefore prepare their application materials and responses in English.

A Spanish version of the call is also available for reference.

No. The programme describes a competitive selection process. Selected applicants will be invited to the innovation bootcamp, after which teams have an opportunity to apply for the Sprint programme and associated funding.

Apply to the AFCIA 2026 Programme

Conclusion

The Adaptation Fund Climate Innovation Accelerator 2026 represents an important opportunity for established organizations developing practical climate adaptation solutions with potential to improve resilience, food security and livelihoods.

Through its partnership with the Adaptation Fund, the WFP Innovation Accelerator is seeking innovations that go beyond ideas and demonstrate evidence of development, relevance to real-world climate challenges, potential for scale and the capacity to create sustainable impact.

The current call focuses on the Dominican Republic, El Salvador and Peru, with priority areas ranging from climate-smart agriculture and disaster risk management to early-warning systems, climate information, water management, climate-risk financing and post-harvest loss reduction.

Organizations that meet the eligibility requirements should carefully assess their solution against the programme’s evaluation criteria, particularly innovation, contextual relevance, scalability, financial sustainability, team capability, climate adaptation, impact, environmental and social sustainability, and gender and inclusion.

item.content:encoded:
Climate Caucus is accepting applications for a Programs & Policy Senior Manager, a full-time, fully remote position for an experienced professional with a strong background in climate policy, policy research, programme management, stakeholder engagement and community-focused climate action.

The successful candidate will help lead research and community programmes that support local climate leadership across Canada. The position combines policy analysis with programme development and implementation, making it particularly relevant to professionals who want to work at the intersection of climate change, local government, public policy, advocacy, research and community engagement.

Climate Caucus describes the position as a highly generative role for a motivated individual with considerable experience in policy development and analysis. The successful candidate will be expected to manage complex and multi-year initiatives, lead policy research, develop strategic relationships with stakeholders and contribute to programmes designed to strengthen local climate leadership.

The position is fully remote, is offered on a full-time contract, and comes with a stated annual salary range of $75,000–$80,000. The currency is not specified in the information provided, so applicants should confirm this directly in the official vacancy notice.

In addition to salary, the position includes benefits such as flexible scheduling, paid time off, healthcare benefits and an annual $1,200 wellness allowance.

The application deadline is August 28, 2026.

About Climate Caucus

Climate Caucus works to strengthen climate leadership at the local level in Canada.

The organization’s work focuses on helping communities, leaders and decision-makers advance practical responses to climate change through stronger policy, programmes, research, collaboration and engagement.

Local governments and community leaders occupy an important position in climate action because many climate-related decisions are implemented at municipal, regional and community levels.

These may include areas such as:

  • Climate adaptation
  • Emissions reduction
  • Land-use planning
  • Infrastructure
  • Public transportation
  • Buildings
  • Community resilience
  • Energy
  • Environmental policy
  • Local economic development
  • Climate-related public engagement

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will help support this broader climate leadership ecosystem.

About the Programs & Policy Senior Manager Position

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager is a senior-level role combining two major areas of responsibility:

  1. Programme leadership and management
  2. Climate policy research and analysis

The position also includes a substantial stakeholder-engagement component.

This means the successful candidate should not only be capable of producing strong climate-policy research but should also be comfortable managing programmes, coordinating relationships, planning multi-year work and translating research into practical action.

The job is therefore particularly suitable for someone who understands both policy and implementation.

Fully Remote Working Arrangement

The vacancy is described as:

Fully remote

This means the successful candidate will not be required to work permanently from a traditional central office under the arrangement described in the supplied announcement.

Remote work can offer greater flexibility, but senior remote positions also require strong self-management.

Applicants should be prepared to demonstrate skills such as:

  • Independent work
  • Time management
  • Digital collaboration
  • Remote team communication
  • Project coordination
  • Accountability
  • Strategic planning

Because Climate Caucus operates in the Canadian climate-policy environment, prospective applicants should also review the full vacancy notice to confirm whether there are any geographic residence, time-zone or Canadian work-authorization requirements.

The information supplied here does not specify these conditions.

Employment Type

The position is:

Full-time

and is described as a:

Contract position

Applicants should consult the formal job advertisement for any additional information regarding the contract term or renewal arrangements, because the material provided does not specify a fixed contract end date.

Salary

The stated salary range is:

$75,000–$80,000 per year

The provided announcement does not explicitly identify the currency.

Because the organization operates across Canada, applicants may reasonably expect the official posting to clarify the applicable currency, but this should be verified directly rather than assumed.

Additional Benefits

The position also comes with a benefits package.

The supplied vacancy information identifies:

  • Fully remote work
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Paid time off
  • Healthcare benefits
  • $1,200 annual wellness allowance

These benefits make the role potentially attractive to experienced professionals seeking both meaningful climate-policy work and flexible employment arrangements.

Main Responsibilities

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will work across several interconnected areas.

1. Managing Climate Programmes

One of the most important responsibilities is managing climate-related programmes.

This is likely to involve coordinating projects from planning through implementation and monitoring.

Senior programme management commonly requires the ability to:

  • Develop programme plans
  • Establish priorities
  • Coordinate activities
  • Manage timelines
  • Monitor progress
  • Support partners
  • Identify challenges
  • Adjust implementation strategies
  • Maintain communication across teams

The role appears particularly focused on programmes supporting local climate leadership across Canada.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate not simply that they understand climate change, but that they can turn climate priorities into structured and manageable programmes.

2. Managing Multi-Year Projects

The position also involves responsibility for multi-year projects.

Long-term initiatives require a different management approach from short, one-off activities.

Applicants may need experience with:

  • Long-term strategic planning
  • Project milestones
  • Annual work plans
  • Performance indicators
  • Partner relationships
  • Budget awareness
  • Risk management
  • Reporting
  • Programme evaluation

A strong candidate should be able to show that they can maintain momentum and strategic direction over extended periods.

3. Leading Research

Research is another significant part of the position.

The successful candidate will be expected to lead research that informs Climate Caucus programmes and policy work.

Policy research can involve:

  • Reviewing legislation
  • Examining government policies
  • Analyzing climate strategies
  • Comparing approaches across jurisdictions
  • Reviewing academic and policy literature
  • Synthesizing evidence
  • Identifying emerging climate-policy trends
  • Producing recommendations

The exact research portfolio will depend on the organization’s priorities.

4. Policy Analysis

The announcement particularly emphasizes policy development and analysis.

This suggests that the successful applicant should have substantial professional experience examining public-policy issues.

Strong policy analysis involves more than summarizing a government document.

Candidates should be able to assess questions such as:

  • What problem is a policy attempting to solve?
  • What evidence supports the approach?
  • Who is responsible for implementation?
  • What are the likely impacts?
  • Which stakeholders are affected?
  • What barriers could limit implementation?
  • How could the policy be improved?
  • What alternatives exist?
  • How can recommendations be translated into practical action?

Applicants with previous experience producing policy briefs, recommendations, reports or submissions may therefore be particularly well aligned with the position.

5. Policy Development

The role is also relevant to candidates who have participated directly in developing policies or policy proposals.

Policy development can involve:

  • Defining problems
  • Consulting stakeholders
  • Gathering evidence
  • Developing options
  • Assessing implications
  • Drafting recommendations
  • Supporting decision-makers
  • Monitoring policy implementation

Because Climate Caucus works with local climate leadership, the successful candidate may need to understand how climate-policy decisions operate at multiple levels of government.

6. Building Strategic Stakeholder Relationships

The Programs & Policy Senior Manager will also be responsible for building and maintaining relationships with important stakeholders.

Climate action often requires coordination across many types of organizations and institutions.

Relevant stakeholders could potentially include:

  • Local elected officials
  • Municipal governments
  • Climate organizations
  • Community organizations
  • Researchers
  • Policy experts
  • Environmental organizations
  • Civil society
  • Government representatives
  • Partner networks

The supplied vacancy information does not list a complete stakeholder map, so applicants should consult the official job advertisement for details.

However, relationship-building is clearly an important part of the position.

Why Stakeholder Engagement Matters

Local climate policy often depends on collaboration.

An excellent policy recommendation may have limited impact if decision-makers, communities and implementing organizations are not engaged.

The Senior Manager therefore needs to be capable of:

  • Building trust
  • Maintaining professional relationships
  • Understanding different interests
  • Facilitating dialogue
  • Communicating complex ideas clearly
  • Supporting collaboration
  • Navigating disagreement

This combination of policy knowledge and interpersonal skill is likely to be central to success in the role.

Supporting Local Climate Leadership

The central purpose of the position is to contribute to stronger local climate leadership across Canada.

Local leadership is essential because climate impacts are experienced directly within communities.

Municipalities and local decision-makers may be responsible for areas including:

  • Transportation
  • Urban planning
  • Building standards
  • Infrastructure
  • Waste management
  • Emergency preparedness
  • Community resilience
  • Land use
  • Local energy initiatives

A Senior Manager working in this field needs to understand that climate action is not simply a national-policy issue.

Implementation frequently occurs at the community and municipal level.

What Does a “Generative Role” Mean?

The announcement describes the opportunity as a generative role.

Although the supplied vacancy text does not formally define this term, the wording suggests Climate Caucus is looking for someone who can do more than execute predefined tasks.

The successful candidate may be expected to:

  • Develop ideas
  • Identify opportunities
  • Shape programmes
  • Generate policy insights
  • Develop new approaches
  • Strengthen partnerships
  • Help determine strategic direction

Candidates should therefore demonstrate initiative and independent thinking.

Ideal Professional Profile

The vacancy is particularly suitable for someone with considerable experience in:

  • Policy development
  • Policy analysis
  • Programme management
  • Research
  • Climate action
  • Stakeholder engagement

Because this is a Senior Manager position, applicants should expect the employer to look for evidence of meaningful professional experience rather than only academic knowledge.

Relevant Professional Backgrounds

The role could potentially be relevant to professionals coming from areas such as:

  • Climate policy
  • Environmental policy
  • Government
  • Municipal policy
  • Public policy
  • Environmental NGOs
  • Climate advocacy
  • Research organizations
  • Think tanks
  • Community programmes
  • Sustainability
  • Public administration
  • Programme management

The supplied announcement does not specify a required university degree, academic discipline or minimum number of years of experience.

Applicants should therefore consult the complete job posting for those details.

Skills That Could Strengthen an Application

Based on the responsibilities described, strong candidates are likely to benefit from skills in several areas.

Climate Policy Knowledge

Applicants should understand the policy environment surrounding climate action.

Knowledge could include:

  • Climate mitigation
  • Climate adaptation
  • Local climate governance
  • Climate resilience
  • Environmental regulation
  • Municipal climate policy

Research Skills

Strong research skills may include:

  • Policy research
  • Literature reviews
  • Evidence synthesis
  • Comparative analysis
  • Report writing
  • Research design

Programme Management

Applicants should be comfortable coordinating complex projects.

Relevant skills can include:

  • Planning
  • Scheduling
  • Monitoring
  • Coordination
  • Problem solving
  • Reporting

Strategic Thinking

Senior-level positions require the ability to consider long-term organizational goals rather than focusing exclusively on immediate tasks.

Communication

Strong writing and verbal communication will likely be important.

The Senior Manager may need to communicate with both specialists and non-specialists.

Relationship Management

The successful candidate should be able to develop productive relationships across a diverse stakeholder network.

Flexible Scheduling

The role includes flexible scheduling.

For experienced professionals, flexibility can support better management of:

  • Work responsibilities
  • Personal commitments
  • Remote collaboration
  • Different meeting schedules

Applicants should remember, however, that flexibility does not necessarily mean unrestricted working hours.

The successful candidate may still need to participate in meetings and stakeholder activities scheduled according to organizational and partner requirements.

Paid Time Off

The benefits include:

Paid time off

The exact number of paid days is not specified in the information supplied.

Applicants should consult the official employment conditions for detailed information.

Healthcare Benefits

The vacancy also includes:

Healthcare benefits

The supplied announcement does not describe the precise coverage.

Candidates should therefore review the full employment package during the recruitment process.

Annual Wellness Allowance

The position includes a stated:

$1,200 annual wellness allowance

This benefit may support employee wellbeing-related expenses under the organization’s relevant policies.

The eligible uses of the allowance are not specified in the supplied information.

Why This Position May Appeal to Climate Professionals

The Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager position offers the opportunity to combine several forms of professional impact.

The successful candidate can work across:

  • Policy
  • Research
  • Programme management
  • Climate leadership
  • Community engagement
  • Strategic partnerships

This combination can be particularly appealing to professionals who do not want to choose between research and practical programme implementation.

The role also provides an opportunity to contribute to climate action at the local level, where many environmental decisions have direct effects on communities.

Application Deadline

Applications close on:

August 28, 2026

Interested candidates should not wait until the final day to prepare their materials.

Given the seniority of the position, applicants should take time to tailor their CV and other materials to the role’s key themes:

  • Climate policy
  • Programme management
  • Policy development
  • Research
  • Strategic partnerships
  • Local climate leadership

How to Apply

Interested candidates should email their resume and a personalized cover letter explaining their motivation and suitability for the role to jobs@climatecaucus.ca.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Application

1. Lead With Climate Policy Experience

Do not make recruiters search through several pages of your CV to understand your relevance.

Clearly highlight:

  • Climate policy
  • Environmental policy
  • Local government
  • Climate programmes
  • Sustainability

near the beginning of the application.

2. Demonstrate Policy Analysis

Avoid simply listing “policy analysis” as a skill.

Provide examples of:

  • Policies you analyzed
  • Reports you produced
  • Recommendations you developed
  • Governments or organizations you advised

3. Quantify Programme Management Experience

Where possible, include concrete indicators such as:

  • Number of projects managed
  • Programme duration
  • Number of partners
  • Number of communities
  • Geographic coverage
  • Budget responsibility

4. Highlight Multi-Year Project Experience

The role specifically mentions multi-year initiatives.

Show that you can maintain strategy, partnerships and delivery across long timelines.

5. Demonstrate Stakeholder Management

Describe your experience working with:

  • Government
  • Civil society
  • Community leaders
  • Policy experts
  • Research institutions
  • Environmental organizations

6. Show Independent Thinking

Because the role is described as generative, provide examples of times you:

  • Designed a programme
  • Developed a new initiative
  • Identified a policy opportunity
  • Created a research agenda
  • Built a new partnership

7. Tailor Your Cover Letter

A generic climate-sector cover letter may be less effective.

Explain specifically:

  • Why local climate leadership matters to you
  • Why Climate Caucus fits your experience
  • How your policy expertise connects with programme management
  • What you would bring to the organization

Important Information at a Glance

Organization: Climate Caucus

Position: Programs & Policy Senior Manager

Employment: Full-time

Work arrangement: Fully remote

Salary: $75,000–$80,000 annually, as stated in the vacancy information

Wellness allowance: $1,200 annually

Additional benefits: Flexible scheduling, paid time off and healthcare benefits

Focus: Local climate leadership across Canada

Key responsibilities: Programme management, policy research, policy analysis and strategic stakeholder relationships

Deadline: August 28, 2026

Application link: https://lnkd.in/dQWRCWRv

Conclusion

The Climate Caucus Programs & Policy Senior Manager 2026 opportunity is a strong option for experienced climate and public-policy professionals interested in helping strengthen local climate leadership across Canada.

The fully remote, full-time position combines climate-programme management with research, policy analysis, project leadership and strategic stakeholder engagement.

The successful candidate will be expected to manage climate programmes and multi-year initiatives, lead policy research and analysis, and build relationships that can support stronger community-level climate action.

The position offers an annual salary of $75,000–$80,000 as stated in the vacancy announcement, alongside flexible scheduling, paid time off, healthcare benefits and a $1,200 annual wellness allowance.

Because this is a senior-level role, candidates should demonstrate substantial experience rather than relying solely on academic credentials. Strong applications should clearly communicate measurable accomplishments in policy analysis, programme management, climate action, research and stakeholder engagement.

Applications close on August 28, 2026.
