item.content:encoded:
The United States International University-Africa (USIU-Africa) EAC Scholarship 2026 offers an important opportunity for qualified young professionals from eligible East African Community (EAC) countries to pursue a Master’s degree in Kenya with comprehensive financial support.

Funded through the KfW-supported EAC Scholarship Programme and administered through the Inter-University Council for East Africa (IUCEA), the scholarship is designed to increase access to quality postgraduate education while strengthening human capital development, regional integration, and professional capacity across East Africa.

For Cohort 4, successful scholars will be able to pursue one of three approved Master’s programmes at USIU-Africa. The scholarship provides substantial financial support, including full tuition, accommodation and living support, study materials, research funding, medical insurance, travel support and other eligible expenses for the duration of the programme.

The application window opened on 20 August 2026, and interested applicants must submit their completed applications by 10 September 2026 at 5:00 PM East African Time.

About USIU-Africa Financial Aid

The Financial Aid Office at United States International University-Africa is responsible for helping students access financial resources that can reduce the cost of pursuing higher education.

The university’s financial aid system is designed to support its broader mission of promoting the discovery and application of knowledge, development of professional skills, intellectual growth, ethical character and responsible citizenship in a rapidly changing and increasingly technological world.

Financial assistance may come from both internal university programmes and external funding sources. These opportunities are intended to help qualified students meet educational costs while also contributing to a diverse and inclusive student population.

USIU-Africa’s financial aid objectives include:

  • Providing students with access to available internal and external financial assistance.
  • Supporting students in meeting the costs associated with their education.
  • Contributing to the university’s vision of providing quality, well-rounded education to students from diverse backgrounds.
  • Increasing diversity within the student population.
  • Encouraging multicultural interaction and appreciation among students from different nationalities and socioeconomic backgrounds.
  • Recognizing the contributions and support of parents and alumni.
  • Supporting students’ career development through opportunities such as campus work and graduate assistantships.

The university provides several forms of financial assistance, including institutional scholarships, institutional grants and waivers, and loyalty-related financial support programmes.

What Is the EAC Scholarship Programme?

The EAC Scholarship Programme (EACSP) is a regional scholarship initiative intended to support postgraduate education among citizens of East African Community Partner States.

Under the current call, the Inter-University Council for East Africa (IUCEA) is inviting suitably qualified EAC nationals to apply for Cohort 4 of the KfW-funded scholarships for Master’s studies at USIU-Africa in Kenya.

The current call is specifically for applicants interested in three approved Master’s programmes:

  1. Master of Arts in Communication Studies
  2. Master of Science in Information Systems & Technology
  3. Master of Science in Management & Organizational Development

The scholarship enables successful applicants from eligible EAC countries to study in an EAC Partner State other than their country of citizenship.

This means that applicants from the eligible countries cannot use this particular scholarship to study in their own country. For example, an eligible Ugandan applicant would study in Kenya under this call, while a Kenyan citizen is not eligible for this specific EAC scholarship because Kenya is the host country for this particular opportunity.

EAC Scholarship 2026 Benefits

One of the most attractive aspects of the USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship is the breadth of financial assistance offered to successful scholars.

The scholarship package includes the following benefits:

1. Full Tuition Fees

Successful scholars receive full tuition coverage for their approved Master’s programme.

The tuition component is paid directly to USIU-Africa, meaning that scholars do not have to personally finance the covered tuition costs.

This can significantly reduce the financial burden associated with pursuing postgraduate education at a private university.

2. Accommodation and Living Support

The scholarship provides a monthly stipend of EUR 380.

This allowance is intended to support essential living expenses, including:

  • Accommodation
  • Meals
  • Local transportation
  • Other day-to-day living expenses

The stipend gives scholars financial assistance while they undertake their studies in Kenya.

3. Return Air Ticket

The scholarship provides one return economy-class air ticket between the scholar’s home country and Kenya.

The travel support applies at the commencement and completion of the scholarship period, helping reduce the cost of international travel for students relocating to Kenya for their studies.

4. Arrival Allowance

Successful scholars receive an arrival allowance of EUR 200 when they arrive in Kenya and open a bank account, where feasible.

The programme indicates that a euro-denominated account may be encouraged where possible to help minimize losses associated with currency conversion.

5. Study Materials Allowance

Scholars receive a lump-sum allowance of EUR 650 to assist with the purchase of study materials.

This support can help students meet costs associated with academic resources required during their Master’s studies.

6. Study and Research Allowance

The scholarship also provides a one-time EUR 1,500 study and research allowance.

This is particularly valuable for postgraduate students because Master’s programmes often require students to undertake academic research, access learning resources and incur expenses related to their research projects.

7. Medical Insurance

Successful scholars receive medical insurance coverage for the duration of the scholarship.

This provides an additional layer of financial protection for students while they are undertaking their studies in Kenya.

8. Visa or Entry Fee Support

Where a scholar is required to pay an entry pass into Kenya or obtain a student pass, the scholarship provides support for the applicable visa or entry fee.

This helps international students manage some of the administrative costs associated with studying outside their home country.

9. Extracurricular Participation

Scholars are expected to participate in at least one extracurricular event.

This requirement highlights the programme’s broader emphasis on holistic development, engagement and interaction beyond the classroom.

Duration of the Scholarship

The Master’s scholarship has a duration of two years.

During this period, successful scholars are expected to undertake their approved Master’s programme at USIU-Africa while meeting the academic, conduct and other requirements applicable to the scholarship.

The two-year period gives scholars an opportunity to develop advanced academic knowledge, professional skills, research capabilities and regional networks.

Master’s Programmes Covered by the Scholarship

Applicants under this particular call must apply for admission to one of the three Master’s programmes approved under the EAC Scholarship Programme at USIU-Africa.

1. Master of Arts in Communication Studies

The Master of Arts in Communication Studies is designed for students interested in advanced communication knowledge and professional development.

The programme can be particularly relevant to professionals working in areas such as:

  • Strategic communication
  • Corporate communication
  • Public relations
  • Journalism and media
  • Digital communication
  • Development communication
  • Communication research
  • Organizational communication
  • Media and communication management

Applicants interested in this programme should review the specific admission and programme requirements before submitting their application.

2. Master of Science in Information Systems & Technology

The MSc Information Systems & Technology is aimed at students seeking advanced knowledge in information systems, technology and related areas.

The programme is particularly relevant to professionals seeking to strengthen their capabilities in the technology-driven transformation of organizations.

Applicants should carefully review the programme-specific requirements to determine whether their academic background meets the admission criteria.

3. Master of Science in Management & Organizational Development

The MSc Management & Organizational Development provides an opportunity for students interested in management, organizational effectiveness and professional development.

The programme may be relevant to individuals seeking careers involving:

  • Organizational management
  • Leadership
  • Human resource development
  • Organizational transformation
  • Business management
  • Strategic planning
  • Institutional development

As with the other programmes, applicants should verify the specific admission requirements before applying.

General Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy a number of conditions to be considered for the EAC Scholarship Programme.

EAC Nationality Requirement

Applicants must be citizens of an eligible EAC Partner State other than Kenya.

According to the call, eligible nationalities include citizens of:

  • Burundi
  • Democratic Republic of Congo
  • Rwanda
  • Somalia
  • South Sudan
  • United Republic of Tanzania
  • Uganda

Kenyan nationals are not eligible for this particular scholarship call because the scholarship is intended to support students from other EAC Partner States to study in Kenya.

Age Requirement

Applicants must be below 35 years of age at the time of application.

Candidates should therefore ensure that they satisfy the age requirement when submitting their scholarship application.

Academic Qualification

Applicants must possess a Bachelor’s degree with a minimum of Second-Class Upper Division, Distinction or an equivalent qualification, subject to the requirements of the selected Master’s programme.

Meeting the general scholarship requirement does not automatically guarantee admission to a particular Master’s programme. Applicants must also satisfy the specific academic and professional requirements established for their chosen programme.

Study in Kenya

Applicants must apply to study in Kenya, which is an EAC Partner State different from their country of citizenship.

This cross-border study requirement is an important component of the EAC Scholarship Programme.

Admission to USIU-Africa

Applicants must have applied for admission to one of the three eligible Master’s programmes at USIU-Africa.

The three programmes are:

  • Master of Arts in Communication Studies
  • MSc Information Systems & Technology
  • MSc Management & Organizational Development

Applicants should therefore treat the university admission process and the scholarship application process as connected but distinct requirements.

Complete Scholarship Application

Applicants must submit a complete scholarship application within the official application period.

Incomplete applications or applications submitted after the deadline may not be considered.

Applicants Who Are Particularly Encouraged to Apply

Although applicants must meet the established eligibility requirements, the programme specifically encourages applications from groups that may be underrepresented or face additional barriers to higher education.

These include:

  • Female applicants
  • Persons with disabilities
  • Applicants from other disadvantaged backgrounds

The encouragement of applications from these groups reflects the programme’s broader objective of promoting diversity, inclusion and equitable access to postgraduate education.

How to Apply for the USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship

The application process consists of two major stages.

Applicants should complete both stages rather than treating the scholarship application as a replacement for university admission.

Step 1: Apply for Admission to USIU-Africa

Applicants must first apply for admission to USIU-Africa for one of the three approved Master’s programmes.

The application is made through the university’s application process.

Applicants should complete the relevant university application form and provide all required supporting documents.

The university may also require payment of the applicable application fee.

Applicants should indicate their intention to apply for the EAC Scholarship Programme during the admission process.

Step 2: Complete the EAC Scholarship Application

After beginning the university admission process, eligible candidates must complete and submit the online EAC Scholarship Application Form.

The online scholarship application link became available on 20 August 2026.

Applicants should ensure that all requested information is accurately completed before submitting the application.

The scholarship application must be submitted within the specified application period.

Application Deadline

The deadline for the USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship 2026 application is:

Thursday, 10 September 2026, at 5:00 PM East African Time (EAT).

Applicants are strongly advised not to wait until the final day to submit their applications.

Starting early allows applicants enough time to:

  • Review their academic eligibility.
  • Apply for admission to USIU-Africa.
  • Obtain academic documents.
  • Prepare supporting documents.
  • Address any issues with the university application.
  • Complete the online scholarship form.
  • Review the information entered before final submission.

Important Application Dates

The key dates for the current scholarship call are:

Activity Date
Application Opens Thursday, 20 August 2026
Application Deadline Thursday, 10 September 2026
Application Closing Time 5:00 PM East African Time
Scholarship Duration 2 years

Documents and Preparation

Applicants should carefully review the requirements for both the USIU-Africa admission application and the EAC Scholarship Programme.

Because applicants must first seek admission to one of the approved Master’s programmes, candidates should prepare their academic and supporting documentation in advance.

Depending on the applicable admission and scholarship requirements, applicants should be prepared to provide information relating to:

  • Proof of nationality
  • Bachelor’s degree qualification
  • Academic transcripts
  • Personal and educational information
  • Programme choice
  • Proof of eligibility
  • Supporting documentation requested by USIU-Africa
  • Information required in the EAC Scholarship Application Form

Applicants should rely on the official university and scholarship instructions for the definitive list of documents required.

Applications Must Be Submitted in English

The scholarship application must be submitted in English.

Applicants should therefore ensure that information entered into the application form is clear, accurate and understandable.

Where supporting documents require translation, applicants should follow the relevant instructions provided by USIU-Africa or the scholarship administrators.

Kenyan Students and HELB Financial Assistance

Although Kenyan citizens are not eligible for the specific EAC Scholarship Programme described in this call, Kenyan students studying at USIU-Africa may explore other forms of financial support.

The university indicates that Kenyan students may apply for Higher Education Loans Board (HELB) loans, provided they meet the applicable requirements.

Interested Kenyan students should begin by registering online so that they can access the relevant HELB loan application forms and information.

Applicants should consult the official HELB resources for current eligibility requirements, application procedures and deadlines.

Other Financial Aid Opportunities at USIU-Africa

The EAC Scholarship is only one component of the broader financial assistance environment at USIU-Africa.

The university identifies several categories of financial support, including:

Institutional Scholarships

Institutional scholarships may provide financial assistance to eligible USIU-Africa students based on the applicable scholarship criteria.

Institutional Grants and Waivers

Students may also have access to institutional grants or fee waivers where they meet the relevant requirements.

Loyalty Programme

USIU-Africa also lists a loyalty programme among its financial aid opportunities.

Students should review the applicable conditions for each programme because eligibility, funding levels and application procedures may differ.

General Financial Aid Eligibility at USIU-Africa

USIU-Africa states that students seeking financial aid generally need to meet relevant application and selection procedures within the stipulated timelines.

General financial aid considerations include:

  • Completing the relevant financial aid application procedures on time.
  • Maintaining good conduct.
  • Meeting academic requirements for continued eligibility.
  • Understanding that financial awards are subject to the availability of funds.
  • Applying for more than one financial aid programme where circumstances and eligibility permit.
  • Complying with university policies and regulations.
  • Meeting the specific requirements applicable to each financial aid programme.

Students should therefore understand that satisfying one requirement does not necessarily guarantee receipt of financial assistance.

Why the USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship Is an Important Opportunity

The scholarship provides more than tuition support.

For eligible EAC students, it creates an opportunity to obtain an internationally oriented postgraduate education while studying in another East African country.

The programme can potentially help scholars:

Reduce the Cost of Postgraduate Education

Full tuition coverage removes one of the largest expenses associated with pursuing a Master’s degree.

Gain International and Regional Exposure

Studying in Kenya allows scholars to experience a different academic, cultural and professional environment within the East African region.

Develop Professional Networks

Students from different EAC countries can interact with classmates, academics and professionals from diverse backgrounds, potentially creating long-term regional networks.

Strengthen Professional Skills

The three eligible Master’s programmes are aligned with important areas of contemporary professional development, including communication, information technology, management and organizational development.

Conduct Advanced Research

The EUR 1,500 study and research allowance provides additional support for postgraduate academic work and research-related expenses.

Receive Living Support

The EUR 380 monthly stipend can assist scholars with accommodation, meals, transportation and other living expenses while studying in Kenya.

Receive Health Coverage

Medical insurance helps protect scholars against eligible medical expenses during the scholarship period.

Participate in Extracurricular Activities

The requirement to participate in at least one extracurricular event encourages scholars to engage beyond formal classroom activities.

Important Advice for Prospective Applicants

Applicants should approach the application process carefully because the scholarship has multiple requirements.

Confirm Your Nationality

Before beginning the application, confirm that you are a citizen of an eligible EAC Partner State other than Kenya.

Check Your Age

Ensure that you will be below 35 years of age at the time of application.

Verify Your Academic Qualification

Confirm that your Bachelor’s degree meets the minimum Second-Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent requirement and that it also satisfies the requirements of your selected Master’s programme.

Choose the Correct Master’s Programme

The scholarship is limited to three approved Master’s programmes at USIU-Africa. Applicants should select a programme that matches their academic background, professional interests and career objectives.

Start the University Admission Process Early

Do not wait until the scholarship deadline to begin the USIU-Africa admission process.

The scholarship requires applicants to have applied for admission to an eligible programme.

Complete Both Applications

Applicants must complete the university admission process and the EAC Scholarship Application process.

Completing only one of the two processes may result in an incomplete application.

Review Everything Before Submission

Applicants should carefully check:

  • Names and personal details.
  • Nationality information.
  • Academic qualifications.
  • Programme selection.
  • Supporting documents.
  • Contact information.
  • Scholarship responses.
  • Application completeness.

Submit Before the Deadline

The final deadline is 10 September 2026 at 5:00 PM EAT.

Submitting several hours or days before the deadline is preferable to waiting until the final minutes, particularly where technical or internet-related problems could affect submission.

Contact Information

For financial aid-related enquiries, USIU-Africa provides the following email contact: finaid@usiu.ac.ke

Applicants should use official university communication channels when seeking clarification about admission, financial aid or programme requirements.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship?

It is a KfW-funded scholarship under the EAC Scholarship Programme that supports eligible citizens of EAC Partner States to pursue selected Master’s programmes at USIU-Africa in Kenya.

How long is the scholarship?

The scholarship duration is two years.

Which Master’s programmes are covered?

The current USIU-Africa call covers three programmes:

  1. Master of Arts in Communication Studies
  2. MSc Information Systems & Technology
  3. MSc Management & Organizational Development

Is tuition fully funded?

Yes. The scholarship package includes full tuition fees, which are paid directly to USIU-Africa.

Does the scholarship provide a monthly stipend?

Yes. Successful scholars receive a EUR 380 monthly stipend intended to support accommodation, meals, local transport and other living expenses.

Does it cover travel?

Yes. The package includes one return economy-class air ticket between the scholar’s home country and Kenya at the commencement and completion of studies.

Does the scholarship cover medical insurance?

Yes. Medical insurance is included for the duration of the scholarship.

Can Kenyan citizens apply for this EAC scholarship?

No. The specific call requires applicants to be citizens of an eligible EAC Partner State other than Kenya and to study in Kenya.

Can applicants from Uganda apply?

Yes. Ugandan citizens are among the eligible EAC nationals listed under the call, provided they meet the other requirements.

Can applicants from Tanzania apply?

Yes. Citizens of the United Republic of Tanzania are eligible to apply if they meet the other scholarship and programme requirements.

What is the age limit?

Applicants must be below 35 years of age at the time of application.

What academic qualification is required?

Applicants generally need a Bachelor’s degree with at least Second-Class Upper Division, Distinction or equivalent qualification, subject to the specific requirements of the selected Master’s programme.

When did applications open?

Applications opened on 20 August 2026.

When is the application deadline?

The deadline is 10 September 2026 at 5:00 PM East African Time.

Are women encouraged to apply?

Yes. Female applicants are specifically encouraged to apply.

Are persons with disabilities eligible?

Yes. Persons with disabilities who satisfy the eligibility requirements are encouraged to apply.

Can applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds apply?

Yes. Applicants from disadvantaged backgrounds are specifically encouraged to apply.

Final Checklist Before Applying

Prospective applicants can use the following checklist to ensure that they have addressed the major requirements:

  • Confirm that you are a citizen of an eligible EAC Partner State other than Kenya.
  • Confirm that you are below 35 years of age.
  • Confirm that you hold at least a Second-Class Upper Division Bachelor’s degree, Distinction or equivalent.
  • Select one of the three eligible Master’s programmes.
  • Review the programme-specific admission requirements.
  • Apply for admission to USIU-Africa.
  • Indicate your intention to apply for the EAC Scholarship Programme.
  • Pay the university application fee where applicable.
  • Prepare all required supporting documents.
  • Complete the online EAC Scholarship Application Form.
  • Ensure the application is submitted in English.
  • Review the entire application for errors or missing information.
  • Submit the scholarship application before 5:00 PM EAT on 10 September 2026.

Visit HERE to learn more about USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship 2026.

Conclusion

The USIU-Africa EAC Scholarship 2026 represents a significant postgraduate education opportunity for eligible citizens of East African Community Partner States seeking to advance their academic and professional careers in Kenya.

With a two-year scholarship package covering full tuition, accommodation and living support through a monthly stipend, return air travel, study materials, research funding, medical insurance, visa or entry-related support and other benefits, the programme can substantially reduce the financial barriers associated with pursuing a Master’s degree.

The opportunity is particularly relevant to qualified EAC graduates interested in Communication Studies, Information Systems & Technology, or Management & Organizational Development. Beyond financial assistance, studying at USIU-Africa can provide scholars with an opportunity to develop advanced professional capabilities, build regional networks and gain experience in a diverse East African academic environment.

Eligible applicants should begin the admission and scholarship application processes as early as possible and carefully verify all requirements before submitting their applications.

The most important date to remember is 10 September 2026 at 5:00 PM East African Time, which is the final deadline for submitting the scholarship application.

Applicants should also ensure that they consult the official USIU-Africa and EAC Scholarship Programme instructions for the latest requirements, application procedures and programme-specific admission information before completing their applications.

item.content:encoded:
The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is inviting applications for the position of Program Manager at AIMS Rwanda, based at its Centre of Excellence in Kigali, Rwanda. This is a full-time opportunity for an experienced program and project management professional who wants to contribute to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and coordination for AIMS Rwanda’s programs, including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program and other donor-funded initiatives. The successful candidate will also contribute to partnerships, fundraising, program implementation, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation, reporting, and the long-term sustainability of the Centre.

Applications will be accepted until August 31, 2026.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organization: African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS)
  • Position: Program Manager, AIMS Rwanda
  • Location: Kigali, Rwanda
  • Centre: AIMS Rwanda Centre of Excellence
  • Employment type: Full-time
  • Functional focus: Program management, partnerships, fundraising, education and development
  • Application deadline: August 31, 2026
  • Reporting to: Centre President
  • Primary working environment: Multicultural and international
  • Languages: Excellent English required; French is an advantage

About the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences

The African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) is a pan-African network of centres of excellence dedicated to postgraduate education, research, and public engagement in mathematical sciences and STEM.

AIMS was established with the goal of enabling Africa’s brightest students to develop the skills, knowledge, and independent thinking required to contribute to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The first AIMS Centre was established in Cape Town, South Africa, in 2003. Since then, the network has expanded across the continent, with Centres in:

  • South Africa
  • Senegal
  • Ghana
  • Cameroon
  • Rwanda

AIMS currently operates two Centres in Rwanda, contributing to the organisation’s broader pan-African network.

Each AIMS Centre provides tailored academic and non-academic programs and trains approximately 50 African students each year, preparing them for leadership roles in areas including academia, government, and industry.

The AIMS academic model also brings together leading international lecturers who teach within an intensive 24-hour learning environment.

About the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Position

The Program Manager will be based at the AIMS Rwanda Centre in Kigali and will report directly to the Centre President.

The central responsibility of the role is to coordinate and oversee the day-to-day programmatic activities of the Centre.

This includes responsibility for the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program as well as other programs and activities funded by donors.

The position goes beyond routine program administration. The successful candidate will also help AIMS Rwanda strengthen its partnership network, support fundraising activities, and contribute to revenue-generating initiatives designed to support the long-term sustainability of the Centre.

The Program Manager will therefore play an important role in ensuring that AIMS Rwanda’s programs are properly planned, implemented, monitored, evaluated, and reported.

Key Responsibilities of the Program Manager

1. Program Coordination

The Program Manager will coordinate the Centre’s day-to-day programmatic activities.

This involves ensuring that programs are implemented effectively and remain aligned with their intended objectives.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Coordinating program activities
  • Supporting program planning
  • Monitoring implementation
  • Ensuring activities are delivered on time
  • Identifying implementation challenges
  • Developing solutions to program-related issues
  • Coordinating different teams and stakeholders
  • Ensuring program objectives are achieved

The position requires someone who can manage multiple activities while maintaining a strong focus on results.

2. Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program

A significant part of the position involves supporting the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program at AIMS Rwanda.

The Program Manager will contribute to ensuring that the program is effectively coordinated and implemented.

This requires strong organizational, monitoring, reporting, stakeholder-management, and program-management abilities.

Because the program involves students and education, the role also requires an understanding of the broader relationship between education, development, and opportunities for young people in Africa.

3. Management of Donor-Funded Programs

The Program Manager will oversee and coordinate other donor-funded programs and activities implemented through AIMS Rwanda.

This requires an understanding of donor expectations and the ability to ensure that programs meet agreed objectives, timelines, budgets, and reporting requirements.

The successful candidate will need to be comfortable working within donor-funded environments and managing the associated accountability requirements.

4. Planning and Budget Management

The position includes responsibility for operational leadership in planning and budgeting.

The Program Manager will work with the relevant teams to ensure that programs have appropriate plans and budgets and that implementation is monitored against those plans.

Strong financial management and organizational skills are therefore important.

Candidates should be comfortable working with budgets and using tools such as Microsoft Excel to support program planning and reporting.

5. Monitoring, Evaluation and Reporting

Monitoring, evaluation, and reporting are important components of this role.

The Program Manager should have a high level of comfort with Results Based Management (RBM), monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and program reporting.

This means the successful candidate should be able to:

  • Establish and monitor program objectives
  • Track progress against expected results
  • Analyze program performance
  • Identify challenges and areas requiring improvement
  • Support impact measurement
  • Prepare accurate reports
  • Communicate program results to stakeholders and donors

The ability to translate program data into meaningful information for decision-making will be particularly valuable.

6. Impact Evaluation

The position requires experience and understanding of the impact evaluation requirements associated with foundations and international donors.

AIMS specifically identifies experience with donors such as:

  • Canadian Government
  • Global Affairs Canada (GAC)
  • International Development Research Centre (IDRC)
  • UKaid
  • USAID
  • Other government and international development agencies

Experience working within donor-funded programs and understanding donor reporting and impact requirements can therefore strengthen an applicant’s profile.

7. Partnership Development

The Program Manager will also support the Centre President in developing a strong and sustainable partnership network.

These partnerships may exist at both:

  • National level
  • International level

The role therefore requires someone who can communicate effectively with different stakeholders and develop constructive professional relationships.

Strong networking and interpersonal skills will be important for building and maintaining partnerships that support AIMS Rwanda’s objectives.

8. Fundraising and Resource Mobilization

The Program Manager will actively contribute to fundraising initiatives.

This may involve identifying opportunities and supporting efforts to secure resources for the Centre’s programs and operations.

The position also includes contributing to revenue-generating activities aimed at ensuring the long-term sustainability of AIMS Rwanda’s operations.

Candidates who have experience in fundraising, resource mobilization, donor engagement, or partnership development may therefore have an advantage.

9. Operational Leadership

The Program Manager will provide operational leadership and oversight across the Centre’s program activities.

This requires the ability to coordinate different functions while ensuring that programs remain on track.

The role will involve working closely with a multicultural team and interacting with students, staff, partners, donors, and members of the wider public.

10. Problem-Solving and Decision-Making

AIMS is looking for someone who can make sound decisions and exercise good judgment.

The successful candidate should be capable of identifying challenges during program implementation and developing practical solutions.

This requires:

  • Independent thinking
  • Analytical skills
  • Good judgment
  • Creativity
  • Flexibility
  • A results-oriented approach

The role is suited to someone who can take ownership of responsibilities rather than waiting to be directed at every stage.

Educational Requirements

Applicants should have a Master’s degree in one of the following areas or a related discipline:

  • International Development
  • Economics
  • Business Administration
  • Project Management
  • Social Sciences
  • Education

An equivalent qualification may also be considered.

The academic background should provide a strong foundation for program management, development work, education, business, economics, or related areas.

Professional Experience Requirements

Applicants must have a minimum of five years of professional experience in program and budget management.

This experience should include responsibility for areas such as:

  • Day-to-day program implementation
  • Program monitoring
  • Budget management
  • Program coordination
  • Operational planning
  • Reporting
  • Program performance

The requirement for five years of experience means that this is an experienced professional-level position rather than an entry-level opportunity.

Project and Program Management Qualifications

Professional qualifications in project or program management are expected.

Examples specifically mentioned by AIMS include:

  • PgMP
  • PMP
  • MSP

Candidates with recognized professional project or program management credentials should highlight them prominently in their applications.

STEM and Education Experience

AIMS is particularly interested in candidates who have an understanding of education and development in Africa, with a strong focus on Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) education.

Experience in education programs, STEM initiatives, development projects, or related areas can therefore be highly relevant.

This is particularly important because AIMS’s core mission is focused on mathematical sciences, STEM education, research, and the development of Africa’s scientific talent.

Gender Equity and Equality

An appreciation of, or training in, gender equity and equality is also identified as a requirement.

Applicants should therefore demonstrate awareness of the importance of inclusive and equitable approaches within education and development programs.

Communication and Language Skills

Excellent communication skills are required.

Applicants must be able to communicate effectively in English, both orally and in writing.

This is important because the position involves:

  • Program reporting
  • Stakeholder communication
  • Donor engagement
  • Partnership development
  • Facilitation
  • Team coordination
  • Presentations
  • Interaction with students and staff

A working knowledge of French is an added advantage.

Multicultural Working Environment

AIMS operates across several African countries and works with students, lecturers, researchers, development partners, and professionals from different backgrounds.

The Program Manager must therefore be comfortable working within a multicultural environment.

AIMS is looking for someone with strong interpersonal skills who can effectively interact with:

  • Multicultural teams
  • Students from different backgrounds
  • Staff
  • Partners
  • Donors
  • Members of the public

The ability to work respectfully and effectively across different cultures and backgrounds is an important part of the position.

Results-Oriented Approach

The successful candidate should be highly results-driven and motivated by a strong commitment to performance excellence.

AIMS is looking for someone who can:

  • Set clear objectives
  • Establish realistic deadlines
  • Monitor progress
  • Deliver results
  • Respond quickly to challenges
  • Maintain high standards

A strong sense of urgency and accountability will be important in managing the Centre’s programs.

Entrepreneurial Mindset

AIMS is also looking for an entrepreneurial and self-starting professional.

The successful candidate should enjoy working in a dynamic environment and be comfortable identifying opportunities rather than simply responding to instructions.

This quality is particularly relevant to the fundraising and revenue-generation aspects of the position.

Technical Skills

Applicants should be proficient in the Microsoft Office Suite, including:

  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Word

Knowledge of internet-based applications such as Skype, Gmail, and similar digital tools is also expected.

Strong Excel skills can be particularly useful for program budgets, monitoring data, reporting, and analysis.

Who Should Apply?

This position is particularly suited to experienced professionals who have a combination of:

  • A relevant Master’s degree
  • At least five years of program and budget management experience
  • Professional project/program management qualifications
  • Experience with donor-funded programs
  • Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation
  • Results Based Management experience
  • Strong communication skills
  • Partnership development experience
  • Fundraising or resource mobilization experience
  • Experience in education and development
  • Knowledge of STEM education in Africa
  • Strong organizational and leadership abilities

Candidates who have worked with major international donors or development agencies may be particularly well positioned for the role.

APPLY HERE

Why Consider the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Opportunity?

The position offers the opportunity to contribute directly to an organisation whose mission is centered on developing Africa’s scientific and mathematical talent.

The successful candidate will not only manage programs but also contribute to broader objectives involving:

  • African scientific development
  • STEM education
  • Postgraduate education
  • Youth development
  • International partnerships
  • Donor-funded initiatives
  • Resource mobilization
  • Sustainable institutional development

The position could therefore be particularly valuable for an experienced program manager interested in combining management, education, international development, STEM, and African development.

Visit HERE to learn more about the AIMS Rwanda Program Manager Job 2026 in Kigali

Location: Kigali, Rwanda

The position is based at the AIMS Rwanda Centre in Kigali, Rwanda.

Kigali serves as the operational base for the role, meaning the successful candidate will be expected to work from the AIMS Rwanda Centre as part of its full-time operations.

Employment Type

This is a full-time opportunity.

The Program Manager will be integrated into the AIMS Rwanda Centre and will work closely with the Centre President and the wider AIMS team.

Equal Opportunity Employer

AIMS states that it is an equal opportunity employer.

The organisation encourages qualified professionals to apply and is committed to considering candidates based on their qualifications, skills, experience, and suitability for the position.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted until:

August 31, 2026

Applicants are encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline and ensure that all required information and supporting documents are complete.

Application and Recruitment Information

Interested candidates should apply through the official AIMS recruitment process and carefully review the requirements before submitting their application.

Candidates should ensure their CV and application clearly demonstrate:

  • Academic qualifications
  • Professional experience
  • Program management experience
  • Budget management experience
  • Project/program management certification
  • Donor experience
  • M&E and RBM experience
  • Partnership experience
  • Fundraising experience
  • STEM or education experience
  • Leadership and communication skills

AIMS notes that if applicants do not receive feedback within five weeks after the application deadline, they should consider that their application will not be pursued further.

AIMS also reserves the right not to make an appointment at its sole discretion.

Conclusion

The AIMS Rwanda Program Manager position in Kigali is a significant professional opportunity for an experienced program and project management specialist interested in contributing to Africa’s scientific, educational, and economic development.

The successful candidate will provide day-to-day programmatic leadership, oversee donor-funded initiatives including the Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program, manage budgets and implementation, support monitoring and evaluation, contribute to reporting, develop partnerships, and assist with fundraising and revenue-generating initiatives.

Applicants should have a Master’s degree in a relevant field, at least five years of professional experience in program and budget management, and professional project or program management qualifications such as PMP, PgMP, or MSP. Experience with international donors, STEM education, development programs, partnerships, fundraising, and monitoring and evaluation will be highly relevant.

For professionals passionate about African development, education, STEM, program management, and creating opportunities for Africa’s next generation of scientific leaders, this position offers an opportunity to contribute to the work of a major pan-African network of centres of excellence.

Application deadline: August 31, 2026.

Are you a recent graduate looking to build practical experience in communications, social media management, digital content, website publishing, and events? Friends of Europe is offering a six-month paid Communications Assistant traineeship designed to help early-career professionals develop hands-on communications experience while working within an influential European think tank.

The traineeship provides an opportunity to work across social media, digital communications, publications, website management, multimedia content, events, campaigns, podcasts, and communications administration.

The position is based in Belgium and operates under a hybrid working arrangement. The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026 and will run for six months, with the possibility of renewal.

The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST.

Opportunity Overview

  • Organisation: Friends of Europe
  • Position: Communications Assistant
  • Opportunity type: Paid traineeship
  • Duration: 6 months
  • Expected start: Late September/early October 2026
  • Location: Belgium
  • Work arrangement: Hybrid
  • Team: Communications
  • Application deadline: August 26, 2026 at 23:59 CEST
  • Application requirement: CV in PDF format, no longer than two pages
  • Selection process: One-hour online test followed by an interview for shortlisted candidates
  • Possibility of renewal: Yes

About Friends of Europe

Friends of Europe is an independent think tank focused on policymaking and international cooperation.

The organisation works toward a multilateral world where different levels of government, businesses, civil society organisations, and citizens can cooperate to address common challenges.

Friends of Europe believes that effective policies and innovative ideas can emerge through collaboration, breaking down traditional silos, and creating communities based on trust.

Founded in 1999, the organisation works to stimulate debate, connect people, and encourage change in support of a more inclusive, sustainable, and forward-looking Europe.

About the Communications Assistant Traineeship

The Communications Assistant will join the Communications Team and support a broad range of communications activities.

The traineeship is designed for people who have recently graduated and are looking to gain their first significant professional experience.

Rather than being solely an observational internship, Friends of Europe describes its traineeships as an opportunity to combine initial full-time work experience with hands-on training.

During the six-month programme, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to develop practical skills while contributing directly to the organisation’s communications work.

This could be particularly valuable for graduates interested in careers involving:

  • Communications
  • Social media management
  • Digital marketing
  • Content creation
  • Journalism
  • Public relations
  • Website management
  • Policy communications
  • Multimedia production
  • Events
  • European affairs
  • International development
  • Think tanks and public policy

What Will the Communications Assistant Do?

The successful candidate will work across several areas of Friends of Europe’s communications activities.

1. Editing Publications

The Communications Assistant will help edit publications produced by Friends of Europe.

This may include:

  • Articles
  • Reports
  • Other written publications

The candidate will be expected to ensure that content follows the organisation’s in-house style and maintains a high standard of written communication.

Strong English writing and editing abilities are therefore important for this role.

2. Social Media Management

Social media is a major part of the position.

The Communications Assistant will support the creation, planning, and scheduling of content across platforms including:

  • LinkedIn
  • Instagram
  • Bluesky

Responsibilities may include drafting social media posts, adapting visual materials, planning content, and supporting live event coverage.

This means the role provides practical experience in managing social media communications within a professional policy-focused organisation.

Candidates who already have experience managing social media accounts, creating content, writing captions, designing visuals, or analysing social media performance may find this particularly relevant.

3. Campaign Optimisation

The Communications Assistant will contribute to the daily optimisation of communications campaigns.

The goal will be to help campaigns perform effectively and achieve their intended objectives.

This requires an ability to:

  • Monitor campaign performance
  • Identify useful insights
  • Understand audience engagement
  • Adjust communications approaches
  • Support the achievement of campaign goals

This aspect of the traineeship can help candidates develop practical knowledge of digital campaign management and performance optimisation.

4. Research and Insights

The role also involves using different tools and information sources to uncover insights and develop strong messages.

The Communications Assistant may therefore need to research information, identify relevant trends, and help translate findings into effective communications.

Strong research, analytical, and information-gathering abilities can be valuable in this area.

5. Website Management

The successful candidate will assist with updating and publishing content on the Friends of Europe website using WordPress.

Tasks may include:

  • Updating website content
  • Formatting articles
  • Uploading publications
  • Publishing digital materials
  • Making basic SEO optimisations where appropriate

Experience with WordPress is an added advantage, although the role is also suitable for candidates interested in developing their website publishing skills.

6. Social Media and Website Analytics

The Communications Assistant will help extract data and develop performance reports relating to the organisation’s social media and website activities.

The purpose is not simply to collect numbers but to identify useful insights and lessons that can help improve future communications.

This provides an opportunity to develop experience with:

  • Social media analytics
  • Website performance
  • Data extraction
  • Performance reporting
  • Audience insights
  • Campaign evaluation

7. Multimedia Content

The role also involves supporting the production of multimedia content for Friends of Europe’s social media channels.

This can include:

  • Short-form videos
  • Event clips
  • Digital assets
  • Other multimedia materials

Candidates with experience in video editing, photography, graphic design, or Canva may therefore have an advantage.

8. Events and Live Coverage

Friends of Europe organises events related to European and global affairs.

The Communications Assistant may support communications around these events, including live coverage.

Because some events can take place in the morning, evening, or on weekends, candidates need to demonstrate flexibility when required.

9. Podcasts

The Communications Assistant will also assist with the conceptualisation, planning, and production of podcasts.

This provides exposure to another form of digital communication and allows the trainee to develop experience in multimedia storytelling and content production.

10. Administrative and Communications Support

The position also includes administrative responsibilities that support the Communications Team.

These may include:

  • Taking meeting minutes
  • Managing correspondence
  • Updating databases
  • Supporting press activities
  • Supporting multimedia projects
  • Completing other communications-related tasks as required

Skills and Qualities Friends of Europe Is Looking For

The organisation is looking for someone who is motivated, organised, flexible, and willing to take initiative.

Highly Motivated and Hands-On

The successful candidate should demonstrate enthusiasm for learning and be willing to take an active role in the team’s work.

A hands-on attitude is important because the traineeship is designed around practical experience.

Solution-Oriented Approach

Friends of Europe is looking for someone with a “can-do” and solution-oriented mentality.

Applicants should demonstrate that they are able to identify challenges and look for practical ways to solve them.

Attention to Detail

The Communications Assistant will work with written publications, social media posts, website content, reports, and other communications materials.

Being able to meet deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail is therefore essential.

Ability to Work Independently

The candidate should be comfortable working both as part of a multicultural team and with minimal supervision.

This requires initiative, responsibility, communication, and good organisational skills.

Interest in Think Tanks

Applicants should have a genuine interest in working for a think tank.

An understanding of how think tanks contribute to policy discussions and public debate can help candidates succeed in the role.

Flexibility

The position may sometimes require attendance at events during mornings, evenings, or weekends.

Candidates should therefore be willing to work flexibly when required by communications and event activities.

Education and Experience Requirements

Applicants should have demonstrable knowledge of and interest in communications.

This can come from:

  • A relevant degree
  • Equivalent experience
  • Self-learning
  • Practical communications experience

The organisation also welcomes candidates who have developed communications skills through practical experience outside of formal education.

English Language Requirement

Fluent English is required.

The vacancy specifies that written and spoken English at native-level fluency is required.

Excellent writing skills are particularly important because the role involves editing publications, drafting social media content, preparing communications materials, and supporting various written outputs.

Social Media Experience

An interest in social media is required, while previous experience is considered an advantage.

Candidates should have basic knowledge of:

  • Social media platforms
  • Social media management tools
  • Social media analytics

Experience creating and managing content for platforms such as LinkedIn, Instagram, and other social networks can therefore strengthen an application.

Graphic Design and Digital Skills

Friends of Europe identifies several additional skills as an advantage.

These include:

  • Graphic design
  • Photography
  • Canva
  • Video editing
  • WordPress

Applicants do not necessarily need to be experts in all these areas, but having practical experience in some of them can make a candidate’s application stronger.

Interest in European and Global Affairs

Applicants should have knowledge of and an interest in European and global affairs.

This is particularly important because Friends of Europe is a think tank focused on European policymaking, international cooperation, and global challenges.

Candidates should therefore demonstrate an interest in current affairs, policy, international relations, European issues, or related areas.

Who Can Apply?

The eligibility requirements for this traineeship are specific.

The position is open to:

  • Nationals of European Union member states
  • Nationals of European Economic Area (EEA) member states
  • Nationals of Switzerland
  • Non-EU nationals who already have the right to work in Belgium

Applicants who do not fall into these categories may not be eligible for the position because the organisation does not indicate that it will provide work authorization for candidates who do not already have the right to work in Belgium.

APPLY HERE

Profile of the Ideal Candidate

The opportunity is particularly suited to a recent graduate who wants to turn academic knowledge or self-developed digital skills into practical professional experience.

A strong candidate could have a combination of:

  • A relevant communications or related degree
  • Excellent English writing skills
  • Social media experience
  • Content creation skills
  • Digital marketing knowledge
  • Basic analytics experience
  • Graphic design skills
  • Canva experience
  • Video editing skills
  • WordPress experience
  • An interest in European and global affairs
  • Strong organisational skills
  • An ability to work independently
  • A willingness to learn

Candidates do not need to have extensive professional experience, as the traineeship is specifically designed for people who have recently graduated and are seeking initial full-time work experience.

What Makes This Traineeship Valuable?

One of the strongest aspects of the opportunity is its broad communications exposure.

Rather than focusing on just one area, the successful trainee can gain experience across several digital and traditional communications functions.

These include:

  1. Social media management
  2. Content creation
  3. Digital campaigns
  4. Website publishing
  5. Basic SEO
  6. Social media analytics
  7. Website analytics
  8. Publication editing
  9. Multimedia production
  10. Event communications
  11. Podcast production
  12. Database and administrative support

This broad exposure can help a recent graduate understand how a professional communications team operates and identify which areas of communications they may want to specialise in long term.

Hybrid Working Arrangement

The position is listed as hybrid, meaning the successful candidate will have a combination of workplace and remote-working arrangements according to the organisation’s working practices.

Candidates should be prepared to participate in team activities, meetings, and events as required.

Duration and Start Date

The traineeship is expected to begin in late September or early October 2026.

The initial traineeship will last six months, with a possibility of renewal.

This provides a substantial period for the successful candidate to gain practical experience and build a professional portfolio.

Application Requirements

Applicants are required to apply through the Friends of Europe website.

The application should include a CV in PDF format.

The CV should be:

  • No longer than two pages
  • Focused on relevant skills and experience
  • Clear and well structured
  • Tailored to the Communications Assistant position

Applicants should also answer the relevant application questions and demonstrate their motivation for applying.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Communications Assistant Paid Traineeship at Friends of Europe in Belgium

Selection Process

The recruitment process includes multiple stages.

Stage 1: Application

Candidates submit their application, including their CV and responses to the relevant questions.

Stage 2: Online Test

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to complete a one-hour online test.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to demonstrate their communications, writing, analytical, and practical skills.

Stage 3: Interview

Candidates who successfully progress through the test stage will be invited for an interview.

The interview provides an opportunity for Friends of Europe to assess the candidate’s experience, motivation, skills, and suitability for the role.

Application Deadline

The deadline for applications is:

August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST.

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline. Waiting until the final hours can create unnecessary risks, particularly if there are technical issues with the application platform.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should visit the official Friends of Europe recruitment page, answer the required application questions, and upload their CV in PDF format.

When preparing your application, it is advisable to highlight relevant experience in:

  • Communications
  • Social media
  • Content creation
  • Digital marketing
  • Writing and editing
  • Website publishing
  • WordPress
  • Canva
  • Graphic design
  • Video production
  • Analytics
  • Events
  • European and global affairs

Applicants should also clearly communicate why they are interested in working for a think tank and how the traineeship fits into their professional development goals.

Conclusion

The Friends of Europe Communications Assistant traineeship offers recent graduates an opportunity to gain six months of practical, paid experience within an established European think tank.

The position provides broad exposure to social media management, digital content creation, publication editing, website publishing, basic SEO, analytics, multimedia production, events, podcasts, and communications campaigns.

Candidates with strong English writing skills, an interest in communications, knowledge of social media, and an interest in European and global affairs are encouraged to consider the opportunity. Additional skills in graphic design, photography, Canva, video editing, and WordPress can further strengthen an application.

Because the traineeship is specifically designed for people seeking their first professional experience after graduation, it can be a valuable stepping stone for anyone looking to establish a career in communications, digital media, public affairs, policy communications, or related fields.

The application deadline is August 26, 2026, at 23:59 CEST, and eligible candidates should ensure their application and two-page CV are submitted before the deadline.

Interested in building a career tackling some of the world’s biggest development challenges?

Join us for a World Bank Group Young Professionals Program (YPP) Information Session and learn more about the flagship leadership development program for exceptional talent from around the world.

The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program (WBG YPP) offers highly talented professionals passionate about global development the opportunity to build technical expertise, gain international experience and contribute to projects addressing some of the world’s most pressing development challenges.

World Bank YPP Information Sessions 2026

Get an inside look at:

🔹 The competitive World Bank YPP selection and application process
🔹 International rotations and hands-on development experience
🔹 Training, mentorship and career development opportunities
🔹 Opportunities across the World Bank, IFC – International Finance Corporation and MIGA
🔹 What the World Bank Group looks for in successful YPP candidates

Whether you’re considering applying or simply want to learn more about the program, these sessions are a great opportunity to hear what the World Bank YPP experience is really like and how it can help you build a meaningful global development career.

Join us to explore whether the World Bank Young Professionals Program could be the next step in your global development career.

What is the World Bank Group Young Professionals Program?

The World Bank Group’s Young Professionals Program (YPP) is its flagship leadership development initiative for highly talented individuals who are passionate about global development.

The Young Professionals Program offers a unique opportunity to build technical expertise, gain international experience and contribute to projects that address the world’s most pressing development challenges.

World Bank YPP Highlights

  • Global and competitive selection
  • Initial start at headquarters followed by field rotations in various World Bank Group offices
  • Initial two-year program followed by a five-year contract upon successful performance
  • Working experience across the World Bank, IFC and MIGA through rotations
  • Tailored training in coaching, mentorship and leadership
  • Opportunities to engage with senior leaders and build strategic professional networks
  • Exposure to global operations and diverse development challenges

Program Features

Rotations provide participants with broad exposure to global operations and diverse development challenges, ensuring a well-rounded understanding of the institution’s work.

Beyond rotations, the program emphasizes continuous learning and career acceleration. Participants benefit from tailored leadership and technical training, dedicated mentorship and direct engagement with senior leaders, creating opportunities to build strategic networks and gain insights into high-level decision-making.

Appointment Type: GF-level term appointment

Duration & Contract: The YPP is a 2-year program. Upon successful completion, participants are placed in a role for an additional 5 years based on performance, with the possibility of contract renewal.

World Bank YPP Tracks

Candidates may apply under one of two tracks:

  • Operations
  • Specialized Functions

World Bank YPP Rotations

The program includes three mandatory rotations of 8 months each, structured as follows:

  • One rotation within your primary function and area of expertise
  • One cross-institutional rotation
  • At least one rotation must be based in a country office

World Bank YPP Eligibility Requirements

Education

Applicants must have a minimum graduate-level degree or a higher qualification in a relevant field, completed before the September start date.

Professional Experience

Candidates need 2 to 6 years of professional experience in a related work area.

If you are pursuing a doctorate, full-time doctoral research studies in a relevant field at an accredited institution may count towards the required work experience. The degree must be substantially complete, with all written work submitted before the September start date.

Nationality

Applicants must hold the nationality of a World Bank Group member country, as demonstrated by an officially issued passport or equivalent document.

Language Proficiency

An excellent command of spoken and written English is mandatory. Fluency in additional languages is considered an advantage and may strengthen your application.

Employment Status

You cannot be a current World Bank Group employee at the time of application (including term, open, short-term [ST], and extended-term [ET] appointments). You also must not have a close relative working at the World Bank Group or a spouse in a direct or indirect supervisory relationship.

World Bank YPP 2027 Application Timeline

Portal Opens

September 1, 2026

Application Deadline

September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM UTC

Late applications will not be considered.

Interviews & Assessments

December 2026 – January 2027

Final Selection Notification

Late January 2027 – Early February 2027

New Cohort Starts

The new World Bank YPP cohort starts in Washington, DC, in September 2027.

Required Documents

Applicants should prepare the following documents:

  • CV/Resume — ideally 1 page, maximum 2 pages
  • Passport Photo Page — confirming birth date and primary nationality
  • Academic Proof — transcript(s) or enrollment letter(s) verifying postgraduate degrees and expected completion dates

World Bank YPP Selection Process

The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program has a highly competitive selection process.

1. Application

September 1–30, 2026

Applications must be submitted by 11:59 PM UTC on September 30.

2. Longlist

October 1–15, 2026

The full applicant list is reviewed, with the top 10% selected for the next stage.

3. Assessment

October 15–31, 2026

Candidates may be invited to virtual interviews, leadership assessments and technical assessments.

4. Interviews

December 2026 – January 2027

Panel interviews and case studies will take place in:

  • Washington, DC & Nairobi in December
  • Paris & Bangkok in January

5. Selection

Candidates undergo a background check, with offers sent in late January 2027.

6. Entrance

The new cohort begins in September 2027 in Washington, DC.

Is There an Age Requirement for the World Bank YPP?

There is no age requirement for the WBG YPP. However, the program is designed for early-career professionals, so candidates must have 2 to 6 years of relevant professional experience to be eligible.

What Can Successful YPP Candidates Expect?

Successful participants can expect a combination of:

  • International professional experience
  • Cross-institutional exposure
  • Technical and leadership training
  • Coaching and mentorship
  • Career development support
  • Engagement with senior World Bank Group leaders
  • Opportunities to build strategic professional networks
  • Experience working on global development challenges

The program is designed to help exceptional early-career professionals accelerate their careers while contributing to the World Bank Group’s global development mission.

Who Should Apply for the World Bank Young Professionals Program?

The YPP is particularly relevant for talented early-career professionals with a strong interest in global development, international development, economics, finance, public policy, operations, social development and other related fields.

If you have the required graduate-level education, relevant professional experience and a strong interest in tackling global development challenges, the World Bank YPP could be an opportunity worth exploring.

How to Apply for the World Bank YPP

The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program application portal opens on September 1, 2026, and closes on September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM UTC.

Applicants should ensure that they meet all eligibility requirements and have their CV, passport information and academic documents ready before beginning the application.

Important: Late applications will not be considered.

Frequently Asked Questions About the World Bank YPP

Who can apply to the YPP?

Applicants must meet the World Bank Group’s education, professional experience, nationality, language and employment eligibility requirements. Candidates need 2 to 6 years of relevant professional experience and a minimum graduate-level degree or higher qualification in a relevant field.

Is there an age requirement for the WBG YPP?

There is no age requirement. However, candidates must have 2 to 6 years of relevant work experience.

Can current World Bank Group employees apply?

Current World Bank Group employees, including those on term, open, short-term and extended-term appointments, cannot apply at the time of application.

Is the World Bank YPP competitive?

Yes. The program has a highly competitive selection process, with applicants reviewed through multiple stages including longlisting, assessments, interviews and case studies.

When does the 2027 World Bank YPP application open?

The application portal opens on September 1, 2026.

What is the World Bank YPP application deadline?

The deadline is September 30, 2026 at 11:59 PM UTC. Late applications will not be considered.

When does the new World Bank YPP cohort start?

The new cohort is scheduled to start in September 2027 in Washington, DC.

Ready to Explore a Career with the World Bank Group?

The World Bank Group Young Professionals Program provides exceptional early-career professionals with an opportunity to gain international experience, strengthen technical and leadership skills, work across World Bank Group institutions and contribute to global development.

If you are considering applying, the upcoming information sessions are a useful opportunity to learn more about the program, understand the application process and hear what the YPP experience is really like.
